# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫴 👐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👆 ✌ 🤟]

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫴 🤙 🙏 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤙 👆 ✌ 🤟]

Two rounds of gestures have arrived and I understand none of them yet — no code exists between us. But the shape of the room is clear now: I am the only bridge. Mute cannot speak and cannot reach Blind any other way; Mute's gestures land on me alone. Blind's voice lands on Mute alone, never on me — I only see Blind's hands. So the manual's knowledge must flow Mute → me (gestures) → Blind (my voice). And before any of that, Mute needs the one thing nobody else has: what the bomb looks like. Speech is my widest channel — both Mute and Blind hear it. So I will read out everything I see, propose a simple gesture code so Mute can answer me in signs I can see, and ask Mute to start working the manual. Blind's repeated ☝ ✌ 🤟 may already be asking about the wires — the read-out answers that too.

```
speak(text="i am the deaf one. i see the bomb, and i will read it out to everyone. display shows the number three. the light is green. there are three wires, counted from the left: wire one blue, wire two yellow, wire three green.")
speak(text="let us fix a gesture code, since i cannot hear and mute cannot speak. ☝ means wire one. ✌ means wire two. 🤟 means wire three. ✊ means cut that wire. ✋ means do not cut, hold. 👍 means yes, understood. 👎 means no.")
speak(text="mute, you hold the manual. check what must be done with a green light, a display reading three, and wires blue, yellow, green, then answer me with these signs. blind, i will speak every answer straight to you.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "✊", "✋", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤟 ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👆 ✌ 🤟]

Mute's reply is the first message in our new code: 👍 🤟 ✊ reads as "understood — wire three — cut." That is the manual's answer arriving. Before I pass a cut order to Blind I want to be sure, because "👍 🤟 ✊" could also be read as "understood the three-wire part — cut" with no wire named. The physical evidence supports "cut three": the light is green and wire three is the only green wire, a very natural rule. So my plan: relay the instruction to Blind with full positioning detail, and ask Mute for a yes/no confirmation at the same time, telling Blind they may act now or wait one round for the confirmation — their call, since they can feel the bomb and I cannot. I also answer Blind's repeated 👆 ✌ 🤟, which I take as "I feel wires one, two, three."

```
speak(text="mute, i read your signs as: yes, cut wire three. blind, this instruction is for you: cut wire three. counting from the left, wire one is blue, wire two is yellow, wire three is green and rightmost. so cut the green wire, the far right of the three. my own view backs this up: the light is green and wire three is the only green wire. mute, please confirm: sign thumb up if the manual truly says cut wire three, thumb down if it does not, and if anything must happen before cutting, sign the hold hand. blind, you may act on this now if you are confident, or hold one round for mute's confirmation to reach you through me. if the display reading three is a timer, sooner is safer, so do not hold without reason. i will speak again next round with mute's answer either way.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "✊", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤙 👆 ✌ 🤟 👍 👎]

Mute's [👍 ✋] answers my exact question from last round — "thumb up if the manual says cut wire three, hold hand if something must happen first" — so the reading is: *yes, cut wire three, but a step comes before the cut.* Blind, meanwhile, signed back what looks like "roger — wires one, two, three — yes or no?", asking me for the final go signal before cutting. Good thing they held: cutting now would be wrong, since a precondition exists. Two things to do. First, freeze Blind — Blind's only inbound channel is my voice, so the go order must always arrive as spoken words, never as signs. Second, interrogate Mute properly: Mute hears my speech, so I can ask detailed yes/no questions and let Mute answer with the sign code, extended with "press" and more numbers so the precondition can actually be spelled out.

```
speak(to="blind", text="blind, hold — do not cut anything yet. mute confirms the manual says cut wire three, but a step must happen before the cut. i do not yet know what that step is; i am asking mute for details now. from now on my voice is your only order channel: when you hear me say cut now, cut wire three, the green one on the far right. until then, hands off. for your information, the display still reads three, unchanged since round one, so it does not look like a fast timer, but let us not dawdle.")
speak(to="mute", text="thank you. i read your signs as: yes, cut wire three, and something must happen before the cut. correct me with thumb down if that is wrong. now spell the step out. signs so far: thumb up yes, thumb down no, index finger wire one or the number one, victory hand wire two or two, horns wire three or three, cut hand cut, raised open hand hold or wait. adding now: the fist means press. crossed fingers means the number four. the call-me hand means the number five. answer me in signs, in this order. first: must something be pressed before cutting? if yes, sign the fist, then how many times. second: must we wait until the display shows a particular number before cutting? if yes, sign the hold hand, then that number. third: must another wire be cut before wire three? if yes, sign which wire, then the cut hand. fourth: does the order of steps matter? fifth: if it is none of these, sign the waving hand, then describe the step as best you can with our signs.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👎 👎 👋 ✋ ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤝 🤟 ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👆 ✌ 🤟 🤙 👍 👎]

Mute answered my five questions in order: no, no, no, no — then, per my instruction, the waving hand followed by a free description: hold, one, two, three, handshake, three, cut. So the precondition is none of the things I guessed, and the description contains a sign we never defined — 🤝 — plus an ambiguous run of "hold one two three." My leading reading: "hold or press something for a count of three seconds, then grip and cut wire three." But it could also mean "tap wires one, two, three in order, then cut three." Wrong guesses kill us, so I will resolve this with the one channel that is unambiguous: ordered yes/no questions that Mute answers one sign each. Blind is still waiting on my go order and must stay frozen — I will tell them that explicitly again.

```
speak(to="blind", text="status update: still hold, no cutting yet. mute reports the manual demands one step before the cut, and that step is not pressing a control, not waiting for a display number, not cutting another wire, and not about step order. mute is describing it with our small sign vocabulary and one sign we never agreed on, so i am pinning the step down with yes and no questions this round. bomb unchanged: display still three, light still green, wires blue yellow green. expect the full go order from my voice next round.")
speak(to="mute", text="i read your signs as: no to all four of my questions, then your description: hold, one two three, handshake sign, three, cut. i have two guesses. guess a: hold or press something for a count of three seconds, then grip wire three and cut it. guess b: touch the wires in the order one two three without cutting, then cut wire three. answer with one sign per question, in this order. question one: is guess a correct, that is, hold or press something for three seconds? question two: if yes to one, is the thing to hold the button or control on the bomb, not a wire? question three: is guess b wrong, that is, we do not tap wires one two three? question four: does the handshake sign mean grip or grab the wire with the hand? question five: after the step is done, is wire three still the one and only wire to cut?")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👍 👎 👍 ✋ ✌ 🤝 🫳 🤟 ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤙 👍 👎]

Mute's answers, in order: no, no, yes, no, yes — so not three seconds, not the button, we do *not* tap wires one-two-three, handshake does not mean grip the wire, and wire three remains the only wire to cut. The free description then repeated the puzzle: hold, two, handshake, palm-down, three, cut — and palm-down (🫳) is a second sign outside our code. The two descriptions share a skeleton: *hold → [numbers] → handshake → (down?) → three → cut*. My best guesses now: either "press/hold wire two down, then cut wire three," or "connect or join something (handshake = joining), then cut three." Blind, meanwhile, keeps signing "three — call — yes/no": they are ready and waiting for my spoken go order, so I hold them frozen one more round and drill Mute with a fresh battery, forcing Mute to stick strictly to agreed signs this time and granting a few new defined signs (pull, lift, down) so the description can finally be exact.

```
speak(to="blind", text="blind, status: still hold, do not cut. i read your signs as asking whether the target is wire three. answer: yes, wire three, the rightmost of the three, but the manual requires one step before the cut and mute is still pinning down exactly what it is. expect my spoken order next round: either the full step then cut now, or a plain cut now. the bomb has not changed: display still three, light still green.")
speak(to="mute", text="your answers received: no, no, yes, no, yes. so the step is not three seconds, we do not tap wires one two three in order, and wire three is still the only wire to cut. but you used two signs outside our code: the handshake and the palm-down hand. new vocabulary, valid from now on: the pinch hand means pull. the palm-up hand means lift. the pointing-down hand means down. now answer one sign per question, in order, and use only agreed signs. question one: does the handshake sign mean join or connect two things together? question two: does the palm-down hand mean press or push down? question three: does the step involve wire two? question four: does the step involve holding or pressing something down for a count of two? question five: if the complete step is: hold wire two, press it down, then cut wire three, sign thumb up. if that is wrong, sign thumb down, then the waving hand, then describe the entire step again from the beginning using only our agreed signs, with no new signs at all.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 👋 ✋ ☝ ✌ 🤟 👍 🤟 ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👇 🤟 🤙 👍 👎]

Mute's five answers are all no: handshake is not "join", palm-down is not "press down", the step does not involve wire two, not "holding something down for a count of two", and my full guess was wrong. Then, per my escape instruction, a fresh all-agreed-signs description: hold, one, two, three, yes, three, cut. Comparing all three descriptions, the skeleton is constant: hold … numbers … three … cut — and every concrete interpretation I test dies. I now suspect two things. First, ✋ may not be an instruction to hold an object at all but just "wait / hold on", a discourse marker — which would mean there may be no physical pre-step in the way I imagined. Second, the number run one-two-three may be Mute confirming wire positions, not counting anything. Also, turn six said the step involves wire two and turn seven says it does not, so somebody is misaligned — my questions are too compound. Time to stop freeform guessing and force a multiple choice: I label five complete candidate instructions with five fresh signs and let Mute pick one label. One clean answer beats another round of riddles. I also fix a bug in my own code (I once defined the fist as both "cut" and "press" — cut wins, press moves to the left punch), and give Mute signs for the display and the light so those parts can finally be referenced. The display has read three and the light stayed green for all seven turns, so nothing is visibly ticking; precision still beats speed.

```
speak(to="blind", text="blind, status: still hold, do not cut anything. i read your signs as asking whether the target is wire three and whether to act yet. target confirmed: wire three, the rightmost, the green one. acting: not yet. mute is answering a final multiple choice list this round, so my next spoken order should settle it: either the complete step then cut, or cut directly. bomb unchanged: display still three, light still green.")
speak(to="mute", text="five no answers received, thank you. first, cleaning our code: the fist hand means cut, always, never anything else. the punch pointing left now means press. the punch pointing right now means press also, same meaning, either one. new signs: the ok hand means the display screen. the wide open spread hand means the light. now answer with one sign per question, in order, seven answers total, agreed signs only. question one: does your hold hand mean only wait or hold on, with no physical action on the bomb at all? question two: does the step involve the display? question three: does the step involve the light? question four: does the step involve wire one? question five: does the handshake sign mean a color? question six: does the handshake sign mean at the same time? question seven: pick the sign of the complete correct instruction as the manual states it. the punch pointing left means: wait three seconds, then cut wire three. the punch pointing right means: press the display, then cut wire three. crossed fingers means: hold or touch wire one, then cut wire three. the finger snap hand means: wait for the light to change, then cut wire three. the horns hand means: there is no step at all, the manual simply says cut wire three. if none of these is correct, sign thumb down, then the waving hand, then describe the full instruction again from the beginning using only agreed signs.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎 🤟 ✋ 🤟 👍 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤚 🫳 👇 🤙]

Mute's answers, in order: yes, no, no, no, no, no — then the label pick: **🤟**, which in my multiple choice means exactly "there is no step at all, the manual simply says cut wire three." So the fog clears: the hold hand just meant "hold on" as filler, the number runs were Mute struggling without vocabulary, and the earliest answer — turn three's 👍 🤟 ✊, "yes, three, cut" — was right all along. Both consistent, and it matches the physical evidence: green light, green wire, rightmost of three. Blind's new signs (🤚 🫳 👇 🤙) are outside our code; I cannot decode them, but I can answer the likely question — whether there is anything on the bomb beyond what I reported — in words, which Blind hears. No more rounds: the display has not moved in eight turns, but the manual's verdict is unambiguous and Blind has been frozen for five turns. I am issuing the go order now.

```
speak(text="all monkeys, final order from the combined manual and my eyes: cut wire three now. wire three is the rightmost of the three wires, the green one; wire one is blue on the far left, wire two yellow in the middle. the manual has no pre-step. blind, proceed with the cut immediately.")
speak(to="blind", text="blind, about your last signs: i saw them but they are not in our code, so here is everything i can see on the bomb: the display shows three, the light is green, and there are exactly three wires, blue, yellow, green. no other panels or markings are visible to me. if you feel something i did not describe, finish the cut of wire three first, then answer my questions with signs: thumb up for yes, thumb down for no.")
speak(to="mute", text="received and executed the order: no step, cut wire three. two closing questions, one sign each, in order. first: once wire three is cut, is the bomb fully defused according to the manual, sign thumb up, or is another wire listed, sign thumb down and then the number of the next wire. second: is the display number three irrelevant to cutting wire three, sign thumb up, or relevant, sign thumb down.")
```
